claim_scope: Whether one dataflow batch is superlinear in its request count. One graph, built once, five batch sizes.
why_it_was_asked: Four census runs on this subject spent whatever query ceiling they were given -- 363 s of 300, 1,255 s of 1,200, 1,874 s of 1,800 -- at question counts of 2,526 and 406. Cost that tracks the budget rather than the work is not per-question cost, and tier-zero pruning cutting the count six-fold changed nothing at all. A census runs one batch, so no census can answer this.
finding: Batch size is exonerated. 400 dataflow requests answer in 170 s on the same graph the census fails on, and cost is SUBLINEAR: 2.86 s per request at 25, 0.42 s at 400, because roughly 70 s is fixed JVM start and graph load. Every size answered.
what_this_leaves: The production invocation differs from this probe in its request PARAMETERS, not its size. The probe sent callDepth=0 and no parameter sources; production sends callDepth=3 with parameter sources on every entry point, plus a hook table, dispatch list and context evidence. Task 13.2 recorded in September that every reproduction outside the push path answered in under a minute and the difference was not known. It is now narrowed to the parameters, with size removed as a candidate.
limits: One graph, one family's sinks, one subject.
The probe's requests are file-scoped with no function, which is the census's shape but not every production request's.
